briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Repeal Momentum Builds in Lansing as Psilocybin and M&A Fuel National Growth
briefs.top: Michigan operators are getting real daylight on the 24% wholesale tax — eight senators now back a repeal bill, both governor candidates are courting the industry, and demand is holding steady despite the hit. Nationally, Compass Pathways just opened its first U.S. office as its psilocybin program heads toward the FDA, while Vireo and Canopy post major growth even as the DEA rescheduling clock gets a short, procedural pause.

local.text: Eight state senators back bill to repeal 24% tax — Sen. Jonathan Lindsey's S.B. 810 calls the wholesale tax nonessential to the state budget and damaging to the cannabis industry, with at least one original yes-vote now flipping in support of repeal.

Demand holds steady despite new wholesale tax — licensed businesses are absorbing the 24% hit rather than passing it to shoppers, with Michigan's 956 cultivators, 275 processors and 835 dispensaries competing hard enough to keep prices from spiking.

Both governor candidates now courting cannabis vote — MiCIA has formally endorsed Republican John James over his pledge to repeal the 24% tax, while Democratic hopeful Chris Swanson has separately vowed to roll it back if elected.

Second lawsuit presses tax-pyramiding argument — MiCIA, grower Mitten Distro X and retailer Refine Michigan are arguing in Court of Claims that stacking the wholesale tax before sales tax illegally pushes the effective rate past the state's 6% cap.

U.P. chain trims to four stores, cites tax directly — Higher Love closed five of its nine Upper Michigan locations, with the company president attributing the consolidation entirely to the new 24% wholesale tax burden.

national.text: Compass Pathways opens first U.S. office in Jersey City — the synthetic psilocybin maker's COMP360 already carries FDA Breakthrough Therapy status, and the company says it's eyeing clinic-based treatment launches in early 2027.

Psilocybin's FDA submission window opens this quarter — Compass Pathways has asked to meet with regulators on a rolling submission for its psilocybin treatment sometime between October and December, a filing that could make it the first classic psychedelic cleared for the U.S. market.

Vireo Growth's M&A spree hits 335% revenue growth — Q2 GAAP revenue jumped to $209.3 million year-over-year, and once announced deals close, Vireo will become the largest U.S. cannabis operator by dispensary count at roughly 270 stores.
Canopy Growth becomes Canada's top medical cannabis firm — the MTL Cannabis acquisition pushes Canopy into the top spot by revenue as the company chases full profitability by 2027.

DEA rescheduling hits a procedural pause, not a setback — the chief administrative law judge stayed the Schedule III proceeding to weigh a new GAO report, with the government's response due October 13 and no finding against rescheduling made.
